chapter_title: Concerning why Some shall delay to come forth from
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation — ¶2

The second [GAP-1: —a condition or degree of spiritual state—] if he shall decline into a lower state [GAP-2: —the manner or depth of the fall into falsity—] one [GAP-3: —a single interior faculty or affection—] one state of spiritual trial [GAP-4: —what transpires within that state—] others who shall [GAP-5: —the function of those remaining truths or affections that are not overthrown—] and they persist. They are held in suspension until they [GAP-6: —the spiritual condition that must be fulfilled before progression resumes—] he is liberated from the bondage of falsity, and they are delayed in approaching conjunction with [GAP-7: —the higher spiritual reality or divine good toward which they tend—].

---

**Translator's note:** This passage is severely fragmented, but its spiritual skeleton is discernible: it concerns a *second case* of spiritual descent — a falling away from interior good into a lower state. During this captivity, certain affections or truths that belong to the same spiritual composite *remain* and *wait*; they cannot advance toward conjunction with the Divine (or with their own higher good) until the one who has fallen is freed. The principle of correspondence here is that of *spiritual solidarity* — elements bound together in one form cannot proceed individually while any part remains in bondage. The "hour" corresponds not to natural time but to a discrete state of temptation. The "delay" signifies the suspension of all spiritual progression that attends unresolved captivity to falsity. The gaps resist confident translation at the natural level, but the spiritual movement — fall, persistence, waiting, liberation, resumed approach — is coherent.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The [sec]ond [case] if he shall fall [into darkness, and] one [of his limbs shall endure] one hour [of bondage, the] others who shall [wait for him] and they remain. They shall delay until they [perceive that] he is freed, and they delay to come toward [the Light]

fills.explanation: The Kephalaia frequently enumerates teaching scenarios as "the first case," "the second case," etc., and "the second" here introduces a numbered scenario of spiritual descent.

The spiritual reading identifies this as "the manner or depth of the fall into falsity," and in the Kephalaia's register, falsity is consistently rendered as "darkness" — the standard Manichaean opposite of the Light; "and" bridges to the next clause about the individual member.

The spiritual reading identifies this as "a single interior faculty or affection," which in the Kephalaia's vocabulary corresponds to one of the "limbs" of the light-soul; "shall endure" bridges to the temporal expression "one hour" that follows.

The spiritual reading says "what transpires within that state" of trial; "bondage" corresponds to captivity to falsity (connecting forward to "he is freed"), and "the" bridges grammatically to "others who shall" in the next clause.

The spiritual reading identifies these as "remaining truths or affections that are not overthrown" whose function is to persist; "wait for him" directly connects to the theme of delay and spiritual solidarity — they cannot proceed without the captive member.

The spiritual reading says "the spiritual condition that must be fulfilled before progression resumes," and the clause requires a verb of recognition linking "they" to the fact that "he is freed"; perception of liberation is the precondition for resumed movement toward the Light.

The spiritual reading identifies this as "the higher spiritual reality or divine good toward which they tend," which in the Kephalaia's cosmological vocabulary is universally rendered as "the Light" — the realm of divine good and the ultimate destination of all liberated light-elements.
